question.html:
Alpha Centauri A and B form the closest binary star system to the Earth. This binary star system is the third brightest stellar object in the night sky.

a

Arcturus is the fourth brightest star in the night sky. Its apparent brightness is slightly greater than that of the star Alpha Centauri A.

Outline why the binary star system Alpha Centauri appears brighter than Arcturus.

[1]

b

Alpha Centauri A is a main sequence star.

The following data are available:

Parallax angle of Alpha Centauri A = 0.76 arcsec

Luminosity of Alpha Centauri A = 5.7 × 1026 W

Luminosity of the Sun L⊙ = 3.8 × 1026 W

b.i Show that the distance from Alpha Centauri A to our solar system is about 4 × 1016 m. [2]

b.ii Calculate the apparent brightness of Alpha Centauri A. [1]

b.iii Show that the mass of Alpha Centauri A is 1.1 M⊙, where M⊙ is the mass of the Sun. [2]

c On the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram,

c.i

plot, with an X, the position of Alpha Centauri A;

[1]

c.ii

draw the most likely future evolutionary path of Alpha Centauri A, labelling the two main regions of this path.

[2]

d Explain how a cepheid variable star can be used for the measurement of very large astronomical distances. [2]
